To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) fusion of simulated GEDI lidars with InSAR data improves the accuracy of biomass estimation, (2) fusion of simulated lidar with InSAR can be used to produce fine spatial resolution biomass maps, and (3) the GEDI data itself may be used to improve the accuracy of InSAR derived height estimates, and thus improve the accuracy of biomass maps.
the fusion of GEDI lidar and TanDEM X In S AR data can improve the accuracy of biomass estimates and that this fusion approach can provide finer spatial resolution.

the fusion of GEDI lidar and TDX InSAR data has the potential to improve forest biomass estimates and to produce biomass estimates at a higher resolution than is currently achievable from GEDI data alone.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing a statistical framework that allows for quantification of uncertainties in forest biomass estimation from multi-sensor data fusion of lidar and InSAR data.
the development of fusion algorithms that can provide accurate biomass maps over large areas at a variety of spatial scales, while quantifying uncertainties in these maps.
the fusion of multi-modal remote sensing data to improve the estimation of ecosystem structure and function, and to quantify uncertainties from the fusion process.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our results show the potential for the fusion of TDX and GEDI observations for improved biomass estimation at a range of spatial scales.
the fusion of TDX InSAR and GEDI lidar has the potential to improve biomass estimation at 1 km, as well as provide biomass maps at a finer resolution than what is achievable by GEDI alone.
the use of Gedi and TanDEM-X data can provide improved biomass estimates at a fine resolution, with uncertainties that can be quantified and propagated in the fusion process.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the GEDI mission is expected to provide high quality biomass estimates at 1 km spatial resolution, while the fusion with TDX will improve accuracies and provide a finer spatial resolution of one hect are.

The main takeaway from our work is that
fusion of data from different remote sensing sensors, with appropriate uncertainty characterization, can lead to more accurate estimates of forest biomass at a range of resolutions.
the use of Gedi observations to parameterize models of other remote sensing data, such as TDX, can improve the accuracy of biomass estimates and provide higher spatial resolution.

fusion of multi modal data can lead to significant improvements in accuracy and resolution, and that the parametric estimation approach can be applied to quantify the uncertainties associated with the fused products.
